sources.title: Log sources
sources.description: Devices that send syslog to the box {{ip}}. The box only accepts logs from the IPs declared here.
sources.caption: Log sources currently received
sources.silentHint: No new line for over 1 hour. Check the device is on, can reach the box, and no firewall blocks port {{port}}.
sources.neverHint: Save the settings on the device, wait 1 to 2 minutes, then press Refresh.
sources.emptyBody: Add the first device or program that sends logs, such as a firewall, NAS, Windows server or web server. Vedette then shows the exact settings to enter on it.
sources.descriptionNoIp: Devices that send syslog to the box. The box address is not known yet: add your LAN range first (Devices, Scope and sensors).
sources.descriptionNoIpLan: Devices that send syslog to the box. The box cannot see its own address in your LAN range {{lan}}, as when it runs in a container: point devices at the address of the machine that runs Vedette, the one you open this page on.

unknown.title: Syslog from an address that is not a source
unknown.notSource: {{ip}} sends syslog over {{proto}}, but no source has this IP, so the box drops its lines ({{times}}, last {{when}}). Add it as a source, or change the sender IP of the source you meant.
unknown.otherProto: {{ip}} sends syslog over {{proto}}, but {{name}} is declared with {{declared}}, so the box drops its lines ({{times}}, last {{when}}). Make the protocol of {{name}} and of the device the same.
unknown.container: On a container install, syslog sent from the machine that runs Vedette arrives from the containers' network gateway (often 172.17.0.1 or 172.18.0.1), not from the machine's own address: declare that address for such a source.
unknown.memory: Counted since the syslog listener last started; the 10 most recent addresses are shown.
unknown.forged: The sender address of a UDP datagram can be forged: check that the address is a device of yours before you add it.

form.addDesc: Choose what will send logs. The next step shows the exact settings to enter on that device.
form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Letters without accents, digits, dashes, dots and underscores, starting with a letter or digit. Example: FW-HQ.
form.ipHint: The box only accepts logs from this IP. Example: 192.168.10.1.

protoHint.udp: The box listens on UDP and TCP and keeps this device's lines from either.
protoHint.tcp: The box listens on UDP and TCP but keeps only TCP from this device: UDP is easy to forge.
protoHint.tls: The box keeps only TLS from this device, on port 6514.

form.added: Log source added. Apply the setup on the device to start receiving.
form.deleteBody: The box stops accepting logs from this IP. Logs already received are kept until the retention period ends. The device configuration is not removed.
form.noMatch: Nothing matches "{{q}}". Try another word, or choose Other device (standard syslog).
form.certHint: Leave empty to accept the device by its IP address alone. To also require the device to present its own certificate, paste that certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint (64 hexadecimal characters; colons and spaces are fine).
form.certBad: A SHA-256 fingerprint is 64 hexadecimal characters, like AB:CD:... or abcd...

config.title: Set up {{name}} to send logs to the box
config.target: The box receives at {{ip}}, port {{port}}/{{proto}}. It only accepts logs from {{sender}}.
config.verify: After saving on the device, wait 1 to 2 minutes and press Refresh: the status changes to Receiving.
config.reads: What Vedette reads from this source
config.noIp: The box address is not known yet. Add your LAN range first (Devices, Scope and sensors). Until then the settings below show {{placeholder}} where the box address goes.
config.noIpLan: The box cannot see its own address in your LAN range {{lan}}, as when it runs in a container. Use the address of the machine that runs Vedette, the one you open this page on: the settings below show {{placeholder}} where it goes.
config.tlsTrust: Over TLS the device must trust the box certificate shown under the log sources (download it there and import it on the device). The box accepts logs from this device by its IP address.
config.tlsTrustPinned: Over TLS the device must trust the box certificate shown under the log sources (download it there and import it on the device), and must present the client certificate whose fingerprint you entered for this source: the box closes any other connection.

bad.title: Connections to bad IPs or domains
bad.description: A device on your network connected to, or tried to reach, an address on a threat feed stored on the box. The box sees this in metadata from a SPAN or mirror port (DNS queries, TLS server names, HTTP host names, flows) or in syslog from a firewall, DNS server or proxy.
bad.descriptionNoSpan: A device on your network connected to, or tried to reach, an address on a threat feed stored on the box. The box sees this in syslog from a firewall, DNS server or proxy.
bad.caption: Connections to bad IPs or domains
bad.listedAsHint: The feed lists this name with all of its subdomains, so the name the device asked for is a bad destination too.
bad.blockedHint: The device that sent this log blocked the connection: the line records an attempt. A device that tries to reach a listed address may still be infected.
bad.empty: None of your devices connected to a listed bad address in the last 24 hours.
bad.emptyFeedsOff: The Feeds module is off, so no connection can be matched against threat feeds. Switch it on under Settings, Modules.
bad.emptyNoIoc: No switched-on threat feed lists any IP address or domain yet, so no connection can be matched. Switch on an IOC feed under Feeds, or wait for its first download.
bad.note: SPAN rows come from metadata only: the box keeps names, addresses and counts, never the content of traffic. Add a mirror port under Devices, Scope and sensors.
bad.noteKept: SPAN rows come from metadata only: the box keeps names, addresses and counts, never the content of traffic.

new.title: New compared with {{days}} days ago
new.description: Log types never seen before from the same source, grouped by type rather than listed line by line.
new.caption: New log types
new.empty: No new log types compared with {{days}} days ago.
new.emptyLearning: No new log types yet. The box is still learning what is normal: {{n}} of {{days}} days of logs so far.

spikes.title: Spikes
spikes.description: Log types that appear far more often than the {{days}}-day average.
spikes.caption: Log types with a spike
spikes.empty: No log type is unusually high.

none.title: No logs to analyse yet
none.body: The digest needs a few days of logs to know what normal looks like. Add a log source, paste the configuration into the device, then come back in 1 to 2 minutes.

events.title: Search events
events.description: Search the logs stored on the box.
events.caption: Log events
events.capped: Only the newest 200 lines are shown. Narrow the time range or add a keyword.
events.found_one: 1 matching line in this time range.
events.found_other: {{count}} matching lines in this time range.
events.partial_one: 1 matching line found so far, searched back to {{time}}. Older lines are not searched yet.
events.partial_other: {{count}} matching lines found so far, searched back to {{time}}. Older lines are not searched yet.
events.searchOlderFailed: The search could not continue. Try again.
events.empty: No matching line. Try a longer time range or remove the keyword.
events.emptyNone: No log line in this range yet. If you just configured the device, wait 1 to 2 minutes and press Refresh in the Log sources section.

retention.title: Log retention
retention.description: Logs past the period are deleted automatically. At the current rate, {{days}} days take about {{mb}} MB.
retention.descriptionNone: Logs past the period are deleted automatically. No log lines are arriving now, so there is no size estimate yet.
retention.label: Keep logs for
retention.shortenBody: Log lines older than {{n}} days will be deleted at the next cleanup (within about an hour) and cannot be restored.

siem.title: Forward to a SIEM
siem.description: Vedette sends a copy of events to your SIEM (Wazuh, Graylog, Splunk, Elastic). Data only goes to the destination you enter here; switching it off stops it immediately.
siem.urlHint: The box sends a POST with a JSON body to this address.
siem.secretHint: Each request then carries X-Vedette-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-Vedette-Signature (sha256=<hex>): HMAC-SHA256 with this key over the timestamp, a dot and the raw body. At least 16 characters.
siem.secretSaved: Saved, ending in {{last4}}. Leave empty to keep it.

event.bad_conn: Connections to bad IPs or domains

siem.noHoneypot: Not on this install: the honeypot needs the appliance install.
siem.sample: Sample of one record that will be sent
siem.adminOnly: Only administrators can change this setting.
siem.cefHint: CEF: 7 header fields separated by |, then key=value pairs.

boxCert.title: Box certificate for syslog over TLS
boxCert.subject: Subject
boxCert.box_ca: Devices must trust the box's own certificate authority (Vedette box CA), which signs the certificate the box shows on port {{port}}. Download it and import it on the device as a trusted CA. Do not pin the server certificate itself: the box replaces it when it renews it or its address changes; the CA stays.
boxCert.self_signed: The box made this certificate itself, so a device does not trust it yet: download it and import it on the device as a trusted certificate, then send to port {{port}}.
boxCert.issued: Another authority ({{issuer}}) issued the box certificate: the device must trust that authority. The file below holds the certificates the box was given; import them on the device as trusted, then send to port {{port}}.
boxCert.fingerprint_issued: SHA-256 fingerprint of the first certificate
